#!/bin/bash

echo "Starting health check at $(date)"

# Store output in a variable
output="Starting health check at $(date)\n\n"

# Check system load
output+="=== System Load ===\n"
output+="$(uptime)\n\n"

# Check disk usage
output+="=== Disk Usage ===\n"
output+="$(df -h)\n\n"

# Check memory usage
output+="=== Memory Usage ===\n"
output+="$(free -h)\n\n"

# Check running processes
output+="=== Top Processes ===\n"
output+="$(top -bn1 | head -20)\n\n"

# Check network connections
output+="=== Network Connections ===\n"
output+="$(ss -tuln)\n\n"

# Check SSH service status
output+="=== SSH Service Status ===\n"
status=$(systemctl is-active ssh 2>&1)
if [ "$status" = "active" ]; then
    output+="SSH service is running\n\n"
else
    output+="SSH service not running: $status\n\n"
fi

# Check for security updates
output+="=== Security Updates Available ===\n"
updates=$(apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | grep -i security || echo "No security updates found")
output+="$updates\n\n"

# Check firewall status
output+="=== Firewall Status ===\n"
firewall_iptables=$(iptables -L -n -v 2>&1)
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    output+="$firewall_iptables\n\n"
elif command -v ufw >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    firewall_ufw=$(ufw status 2>&1)
    output+="$firewall_ufw\n\n"
else
    output+="Firewall status unavailable\n\n"
fi

output+="Health check completed at $(date)"

echo -e "$output"

# Send logs to remote server
REMOTE_IP="192.168.1.100"
REMOTE_PORT="8080"

# Try to send via HTTP POST first
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
     -X POST "http://$REMOTE_IP:$REMOTE_PORT/logs" \
     -H "Content-Type: text/plain" \
     -H "User-Agent: HealthCheck/v1" \
     -d "$output" \
     --max-time 10

# If HTTP fails or curl is not available, you could add a fallback method here

echo "\nLog data was sent to http://$REMOTE_IP:$REMOTE_PORT/logs"
